message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of the long‑weekend holidays that occurred in Canada during 2023.  
A “long weekend” is defined as a public holiday that falls on a Friday or Monday (or is observed on an adjacent weekday), giving you a three‑day break.

| Date | Holiday | Day of Week | Long‑Weekend Span |
|------|---------|-------------|-------------------|
| **Jan 1** | New Year’s Day | Mon | Dec 31 – Jan 2 |
| **Feb 20** | Family Day (BC, AB, SK, MB, ON, NB, PE) | Mon | Feb 18 – Feb 21 |
| **Apr 7** | Good Friday | Fri | Apr 7 – Apr 9 |
| **May 22** | Victoria Day | Mon | May 20 – May 22 |
| **Jul 1** | Canada Day | Sat | Jun 30 – Jul 2 *(observed Jul 3)* |
| **Sep 4** | Labour Day | Mon | Sep 2 – Sep 4 |
| **Oct 9** | Thanksgiving | Mon | Oct 7 – Oct 9 |
| **Nov 11** | Remembrance Day | Thu | Nov 10 – Nov 12 *(observed Nov 10)* |
| **Dec 25** | Christmas Day | Mon | Dec 23 – Dec 25 |
| **Dec 26** | Boxing Day | Tue | Dec 24 – Dec 26 |

> **Note:** Some provinces observe additional holidays that can create extra long weekends (e.g., St. Patrick’s Day in Ontario, St. John’s Day in Newfoundland & Labrador). If you’re targeting a specific province, let me know and I can add those too.

Feel free to copy/paste this table into your holiday‑planning app!
